A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SageAttention work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite pagination changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original GPU speed measurements, model evaluations, quantization studies and qualitative generation results in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices A–B, including speed comparisons, accuracy evaluations and ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.6 and Algorithm 1 retain the same K smoothing, quantization choices, FP16 accumulation, adaptive kernel selection and fusion procedures. The appendix reorganization introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same language, image/video generation, classification and visual-question-answering tasks, datasets and qualitative examples. The additional application areas suggested in v5 Appendix A.6 are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Torch, xformers and FlashAttention2 in speed comparisons; full precision and FlashAttention3 in accuracy comparisons; and AWQ, Q-diffusion and ViDiT-Q in Tables 13–15. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain RTX4090/3090 testing, head dimensions 64/128, causal and noncausal configurations, identical metrics and the first 256 COCO 2014 validation examples. Section 5 and Appendix A.1–A.3 report no revised evaluation settings.

E4.justification: The datatype and accumulator studies, K-smoothing comparisons, adaptive-quantization ablation and qualitative generation examples are retained unchanged. This includes Tables 1–5, 10–11 and 17–18, and Figures 10–14.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point estimates and average/worst-layer summaries. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical tables, speed plots and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 7 retains the 2.01x CogvideoX attention speedup on RTX4090, and Table 8 retains Llama2 WikiText perplexities of 5.823 for full precision and 5.824 for SageAttention.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, quantizer definitions, online-softmax mathematics and the argument that subtracting mean(K) preserves attention probabilities are unchanged. The appendices introduce no new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: plug-and-play quantized attention, accuracy-preserving acceleration and approximately 2.1x/2.7x speed advantages over FlashAttention2/xformers.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 newly suggests applicability to MoE, RAG, training optimization, heterogeneous GPU systems and other applications without additional validation. Section 6 removes v3's statement leaving Hopper implementation to future work; this does not establish that Hopper support was implemented. Existing explanations of experimental results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds an explicit SageAttention implementation-repository link in the abstract, absent from v3. Hardware, software versions, kernel hyperparameters and data/model preparation details in Appendix A.1–A.3 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds citations connecting SageAttention to possible applications, including MoA, SageAttention2, ReMoE, training/serving systems and diffusion work. These broaden contextual connections, while Section 2's attention taxonomy, central positioning and distinctions from competing methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 expands affiliations, adds a corresponding-author note and acknowledgments, separates the fusion and performance-analysis paragraphs, and reorganizes A.7–A.10 as B and B.1–B.3. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v5 adds conference running headers and adjusts text coloring, spacing and placement of existing material. Added references and prose cause reflow, but Figures 1–14 and Tables 1–19 retain their content and display structures.

improvement.justification: The abstract's new implementation-repository link provides a modest improvement in reproducibility guidance over v3. Scientific evidence and technical details are unchanged. The new application suggestions add little substantiation, and removing the Hopper future-work qualification slightly reduces scope clarity, so the net improvement is limited.
